g.text: Colour: which part of the architecture a box belongs to
Why: who cares (stakeholders), and the drivers, goals, outcomes, values and requirements
Strategy: what the organisation is able to do (capabilities) and with what (resources, value streams)
Software: systems and their parts, the services they offer, and the data they hold
Shape: what kind of thing a box is (its small italic label names the exact kind)
Cut corners: a reason or aim, such as a stakeholder, goal, outcome or value
Rounded corners: something done or an ability, such as a capability, process or function
Rounded ends: a service, offered for others to use
Square corners: something that exists, such as a system, a role, or a piece of data
A box inside another box: a part of it
Grey band: a grouping for layout only; it adds no meaning
Line: how two boxes are related, read from where the line starts to where it ends
Flow: passes something, such as information, to
Association: is related to (no more specific meaning)
